title: The convolution of the Fourier kernels is the delta kernel
statement:
Fix distinct primes $p,\ell$, $a\geq1$, $q=p^a$, $k_0=\mathbf F_q$ and $k=\overline{k_0}$, in the Fourier conventions [def-fourier-set]. Fix a nontrivial character $\Psi:(\mathbf F_p,+)\to\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell^\times$ and write $\psi=\Psi\circ\operatorname{Tr}_{k_0/\mathbf F_p}$. Over $k$ the notation $\mathcal L_{\psi,f}$ means the geometric pullback of the prime-field Artin–Schreier sheaf attached to $\Psi$ and $f$ [def-fd-artin-schreier-sheaf], not a trace from $k$ to $\mathbf F_p$. Work in $D^b_c(-,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell)$ with the adic common-stage coefficients of [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]. Let $S=\operatorname{Spec}k$, $r\geq0$, $V=\mathbf A^r_k$ and $V^\vee$ its dual. Use the Fourier kernels [def-fd-kernel] of the evaluation pairings on $V\times V^\vee$ and $V^\vee\times V$, and the unshifted convolution $\ast$ of [lem-fd-kernel-composition]. Then
$$
\mathcal K_{\psi^{-1}}\ast\mathcal K_\psi\cong\Delta_*\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell(-r)[-2r],\qquad
\mathcal K_\psi\ast\mathcal K_\psi\cong(\operatorname{id}_V\times\iota')_*\Delta_*\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell(-r)[-2r],
$$
where $\Delta:V\to V\times_kV$ sends $x$ to $(x,x)$, $\iota':V\to V$ sends $y$ to $-y$, and the twists are [def-coefficient-twists-detailed]. All sheaves and maps are the geometric pullbacks from their indicated finite-field models.

proof.text: Put $B=V\times_kV$, $T=V\times_kV^\vee\times_kV$ and $P=r_{13}:T\to B$. Define $C_-$ and $C_+$ to be the two convolutions in the statement. The convolution formula of [lem-fd-kernel-composition] and the pullback description of [def-fd-kernel] give their integrands as the tensor products of the two evaluation sheaves. By the multiplicativity and inverse identities of [lem-fd-as-lisse], these are respectively $\mathcal L_{\psi,\langle\xi,x-y\rangle}$ and $\mathcal L_{\psi,\langle\xi,x+y\rangle}$. Thus, putting $c_-=x-y$, $c_+=x+y$ and $F_\pm=\mathcal L_{\psi,\langle\xi,c_\pm\rangle}$, one has $C_\pm=RP_!F_\pm$. These are bounded constructible complexes by the stability clause (8) of [sk-thm-sf-package]: the evaluation sheaves are rank-one lisse and have finite Tor amplitude by [prop-kernel-lisse]. All projections are separated finite type between separated finite-type $k$-schemes. The calculation below is the unit's fibre calculation carried out over relative coordinate charts; in particular it does not assume that arbitrary geometric points have residue field $k$.

source.place: first paragraph: identify the two kernel factors and their tensor product

proof.text: To relate this family calculation to the unit's Fourier stalk formula, fix $y\in V(k)$ and put $K_{-,y}(\xi)=\mathcal L_{\psi^{-1},\langle\xi,y\rangle}$, $K_{+,y}(\xi)=\mathcal L_{\psi,\langle\xi,y\rangle}$ on $V^\vee$. These are rank-one lisse bounded constructible objects. Apply [thm-cbc-qbar] to $P$ along the slice $s_y:V\to B$, $x\mapsto(x,y)$. Under the symmetry $V\times V^\vee\cong V^\vee\times V$, [def-fd-transform] gives $s_y^*C_\pm\cong\operatorname{FT}_\psi(K_{\pm,y})[-r]$, the transform now having input $V^\vee$ and output its bidual $V$. The shift $[r]$ in that definition is cancelled explicitly. Apply [lem-fd-stalk-formula] to these actual transform objects: for $\bar x:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to V$ the result is $R\Gamma_c(\mathbf A^r_\Omega,\mathcal L_{\psi,\langle\xi,x-y\rangle})$ for $C_-$ and the same with $x+y$ for $C_+$. The linear-function sheaf identities are those of Step 1. We will prove the vanishing and the constant closed restriction relatively, rather than glue these pointwise identifications; this also handles pairs whose second coordinate is not k-rational.

source.place: first paragraph: the same stalk computation as the Fourier stalk formula, applied to actual fixed-y transform objects

proof.text: Let $L=\mathcal L_{\psi,t}$ on $\mathbf A^1_k$. By [lem-fd-as-lisse] it is lisse of rank one with coefficient dual $L^\vee=\mathcal L_{\psi,-t}$. It is site-perfect: on the finite etale Artin–Schreier trivializing cover it is a free rank-one coefficient module in degree zero, exactly [def-pod-perfect-complex-on-x]. The curve $\mathbf A^1_{k_0}$ is smooth, separated, geometrically connected of dimension one and descends to the finite field; properness is not required in [thm-pod-degreewise-perfectness-over-a-field]. Apply that theorem at $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ to obtain $H_c^i(\mathbf A^1_k,L)^\vee\cong H^{2-i}(\mathbf A^1_k,\mathcal L_{\psi,-t}(1))$. The right side vanishes by [lem-fd-cohomology-affine-line-character] with nonzero scalar $-1$; tensoring with the one-dimensional constant twist on the algebraically closed point preserves zero. Negative ordinary degrees also vanish for a sheaf in degree zero. The compact cohomology groups are finite-dimensional by the duality theorem, so a zero dual forces each of them to vanish. Consequently $R\Gamma_c(\mathbf A^1_k,L)=0$.

source.place: second paragraph: deduce compact-support vanishing from ordinary cohomology and degreewise duality

proof.text:
For either sign let $Z_\pm\subset B$ be the closed subscheme defined by the $r$ equations $c_{\pm,j}=0$, and put $U_\pm=B\setminus Z_\pm$. If $r>0$, the $r$ principal opens $U_{\pm,i}=D(c_{\pm,i})$ cover $U_\pm$. On $U_{\pm,i}$ set $t=\sum_j c_{\pm,j}\xi_j$ and $u_j=\xi_j$ for $j
e i$. The inverse change of coordinates is $\xi_i=c_{\pm,i}^{-1}(t-\sum_{j
e i}c_{\pm,j}u_j)$, $\xi_j=u_j$ for $j
e i$. Both maps are regular on this principal open, and substituting gives the identity in either direction. This identifies $T|_{U_{\pm,i}}$ with $\mathbf A^1_{U_{\pm,i}}	imes\mathbf A^{r-1}$ and $F_\pm$ with the pullback of $\mathcal L_{\psi,t}$ along the first projection, by [def-fd-kernel]'s pullback rule. When $r=0$, $Z_\pm=B$ and $U_\pm$ is empty; no rank $-1$ is used.

source.place: first paragraph: choose a coordinate given by the nonzero linear form; relative chart version with explicit inverse

proof.text: Fix one chart $W=U_{\pm,i}$ and write $\rho:\mathbf A^r_W\to\mathbf A^1_W$, $a:\mathbf A^1_W\to W$ and $b:W\to\operatorname{Spec}k$. Compact-support base change [thm-cbc-qbar] identifies $C_\pm|_W$ with $R(a\rho)_!\rho^*L_W$, where $L_W$ is the pullback of $L$ from $\mathbf A^1_k$. The composition law of [sk-thm-sf-package](4) and the projection formula [fix-prop-projection-formula] give $R(a\rho)_!\rho^*L_W\cong Ra_!(L_W\otimes R\rho_!\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell)$. Here $\rho$ is a trivial bundle of rank $r-1$; [lem-fd-affine-space-thom-coefficient-transport] identifies its compact-support constant image with $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell(-(r-1))[-2(r-1)]$. Applying the projection formula to the twist pulled back from $W$ then gives $C_\pm|_W\cong(Ra_!L_W)(-(r-1))[-2(r-1)]$. In the cartesian square obtained from $\mathbf A^1_k\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ by $b$, [thm-cbc-qbar] identifies $Ra_!L_W$ with $b^*R\Gamma_c(\mathbf A^1_k,L)$, which is zero by Step 3. All schemes in these squares are noetherian, finite-dimensional and have $\ell$ invertible; every compact-support map is separated finite type. The rank-one sheaf and the twists are in the finite-Tor domains of the projection formula.

source.place: first paragraph: projection formula and the transported Thom computation off the vanishing locus

proof.text: The chartwise zero objects imply $C_\pm|_{U_\pm}=0$ in the adic common-stage category, as follows. By [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients], the object and the finitely many identities expressing that its restrictions are zero are represented after one common finite coefficient extension $E$. Choose an integral representative $M\in D^b_c(U_\pm,\mathcal O_E)$. Its restriction to each chart is zero after inverting $\varpi_E$. Apply [lem-sf-rational-local-global-power-torsion] to this finite open cover: one power $\varpi_E^N$ kills every cohomology sheaf of $M$. Choose a bounded cohomological interval $[u,v]$ for $M$ and apply [lem-sf-rational-bounded-cone-torsion]. It gives $\varpi_E^{N(v-u+2)}\operatorname{id}_M=0$, hence $M_E=0$ and therefore $C_\pm|_{U_\pm}=0$. For empty $U_\pm$ the same lemmas allow the empty covering, or the assertion follows directly from the zero sheaf category on the empty scheme.

source.place: second paragraph, support claim: passage from relative chart vanishing to vanishing on the entire open complement

proof.text: Let $i_\pm:Z_\pm\hookrightarrow B$. The base-changed map $P_Z:T\times_BZ_\pm\to Z_\pm$ is the trivial rank-$r$ bundle with coordinates $\xi$. On $Z_-$ one has $y=x$, so the original two evaluation factors are tensor inverses; on $Z_+$ one has $y=-x$, so the same is true of the two same-character factors. The inverse identity of [lem-fd-as-lisse] gives in both cases the unit sheaf on the whole $T\times_BZ_\pm$, not just a unit at its individual points. Applying [thm-cbc-qbar] along $i_\pm$, followed by [lem-fd-affine-space-thom-coefficient-transport] with $Y=Z_\pm$ and $m=r$, gives $i_\pm^*C_\pm\cong RP_{Z!}\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell\cong\overline{\mathbf Q}_{\ell,Z_\pm}(-r)[-2r]$. This is a relative identification of complexes on $Z_\pm$. The bases are isomorphic to $V$, so they meet all finite-type and separatedness hypotheses; rank zero is the identity normalization of the transported Thom statement.

source.place: second paragraph: the integrand is constant on the vanishing locus, and the same Thom isomorphism identifies its relative direct image

proof.text: Apply [prop-sf-open-closed-triangle-all-stages] at $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ to $C_\pm$ and the closed-open pair $(i_\pm,j_\pm)$. Its triangle is $j_{\pm!}j_\pm^*C_\pm\to C_\pm\to i_{\pm*}i_\pm^*C_\pm\to$. Step 6 makes the first term zero, so the specified middle unit map is an isomorphism. Step 7 therefore gives $C_\pm\cong i_{\pm*}\overline{\mathbf Q}_{\ell,Z_\pm}(-r)[-2r]$. Explicitly $Z_-\cong V$ via $x\mapsto(x,x)$ and $Z_+\cong V$ via $x\mapsto(x,-x)$; the inverse is the first projection, and the equations $x-y=0$ and $x+y=0$ verify these scheme isomorphisms. Hence $i_-=\Delta$ and $i_+=(\operatorname{id}\times\iota')\Delta$. The direct-image composition law for these proper maps, equivalently compact-support composition and proper coincidence in [sk-thm-sf-package](4), yields exactly the two displayed identities. In characteristic two $Z_+=Z_-$, as it should; when $r=0$ both identities reduce to the unit on a point.

source.place: second paragraph: replace the unsupported stalkwise identification by the actual open-closed unit isomorphism; diagonal and anti-diagonal conclusions

proof_origin.place: Entire proof, completed by relative charts, coefficient transport, restriction to the closed support and open-closed localization; the unit route is unchanged.
